source_user: Calculation case 32: a model has 32 layers, 8 KV heads, head dimension 96, sequence length 2560, and BF16/FP16 KV values. Estimate bytes for one request's K/V cache. Show the formula and report GiB.
source_assistant: Use 2 × layers × sequence_length × KV_heads × head_dim × bytes_per_value. Here this is 2 × 32 × 2560 × 8 × 96 × 2 = 251658240 bytes = 0.234375 GiB. This excludes allocator metadata and other runtime memory.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions that must hold for this number to be meaningful: exactly one request, GQA/MQA layout where 8 is the number of KV heads (num_key_value_heads) and NOT query heads, dense attention in every one of the 32 decoder layers, no sliding-window or layer-skipping KV sharing, no cross-attention, and the full 2560 tokens resident simultaneously.

Mechanism: each decoder layer caches one K tensor and one V tensor per token. Per token per layer the footprint is kv_heads x head_dim x bytes_per_value for K plus the same for V, hence the leading factor 2. Multiplying across layers and sequence length gives the closed form:

  bytes = 2 x layers x sequence_length x kv_heads x head_dim x bytes_per_value
        = 2 x 32 x 2560 x 8 x 96 x 2
        = 251658240 bytes
        = 251658240 / 1073741824 = 0.234375 GiB

Per-token cost is 2 x 32 x 8 x 96 x 2 = 98304 bytes/token, which is the number to use for admission control and for extrapolating to other context lengths; it scales linearly in sequence length, so doubling context doubles this figure exactly. Because dtype is BF16/FP16, bytes_per_value=2 and there is no scale/zero-point side channel.

Boundary conditions where the estimate is wrong: (a) paged KV engines such as vLLM allocate in blocks (commonly 16 tokens), so real usage rounds up to ceil(2560/block_size) x block_size tokens per sequence, and prefix-cache sharing can make aggregate usage lower than N x this value; (b) tensor parallelism shards KV heads across ranks, so per-GPU usage is roughly this divided by TP degree only when kv_heads is divisible by TP degree, otherwise KV heads are replicated and per-GPU usage is higher; (c) this excludes weights, activation and workspace buffers, CUDA graph pools, and allocator fragmentation, which together commonly consume more than the KV cache at low concurrency.

Falsifiable prediction: on the target engine, raising concurrency from 1 to N identical 2560-token requests should increase steady-state KV-block occupancy by approximately N x ceil(2560/block_size) blocks and reserved memory by approximately N x 0.234375 GiB (minus any shared prefix blocks). If measured growth deviates by more than ~10% after accounting for block rounding, the assumed config (kv_heads, head_dim, layers, or KV dtype) is wrong and must be re-read from the served model rather than from the prompt.

Rollback gate: do not raise max_num_seqs or max_model_len on the basis of this arithmetic alone. Require a controlled ramp showing peak reserved memory <= 85-90% of device memory with headroom for the longest admitted request; if any preemption/recompute events or OOM appear during the ramp, revert to the previous concurrency and context limits immediately.
risks: Formula omits paged-KV block rounding and allocator fragmentation; sizing concurrency directly from it can trigger OOM or preemption under load.
Uses KV heads rather than query heads; misapplying it to an MHA checkpoint understates KV memory by the GQA group factor.
Ignores tensor-parallel KV-head replication when num_key_value_heads is not divisible by the TP degree, so per-GPU usage can exceed total/TP.
